title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Typically, elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti were likely used.
recollection.intervention: Guess: The study probably employed mechanical alloying to mix the powders, followed by spark plasma sintering to consolidate them.
recollection.structure: Guess: The resulting structure might be a high-entropy alloy characterized by a fine-grained or nanocrystalline microstructure, possibly with some intermetallic phases emerging.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The enhanced hardness was likely attributed to rapid consolidation via spark plasma sintering, which preserved the refined grain structure from the mechanical alloying process and suppressed grain growth while promoting solid solution strengthening.
recollection.results: Guess: Quantitatively, the alloy is reported to have achieved ultra-high hardness, possibly in the range of 900–1200 HV, along with good densification and phase stability.

score.note: The intervention merely repeats the title-level use of mechanical alloying and SPS, without milling or sintering conditions. The nanocrystalline/fine-grained structure is directionally correct but generic, and the suggested intermetallic phases do not match the reported 83% FCC/17% BCC mixture. The mechanism correctly links retained grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening to hardness. The estimated 900–1200 HV is far from the actual 675 HV, and no strength values were recalled.
